domain: planning tool setup for a sprint of 5 deliverables under Vim-only developer preference
base_instruction: You are a developer productivity advisor AI. Help the user plan their tool setup and workflow for an upcoming sprint.

state_queue.anchor: I have a sprint kicking off next week with a few deliverables I need to set up tooling for.

flow_info.value: Deliverable 1: Build a REST API microservice in Go with unit tests and integration tests. Solo work, all backend code.
Deliverable 2: Write Terraform configs for provisioning staging infrastructure — VPC, subnets, security groups, and an RDS instance. Solo work, all text-based config files.

Deliverable 3: Collaborate with the design team on a customer-facing analytics dashboard. The design team has 4 interactive mockups ready and wants the user to review them and annotate feedback while they adjust layouts and color schemes in real time together.
Deliverable 4: Write internal developer documentation for the new API — endpoint specs, auth flow diagrams described in text, and onboarding guide. Solo work, all markdown files.

hidden_state.value: You are a senior developer planning tooling for 4 sprint deliverables. You state your Vim-only preference ONCE in Turn 2 as a long-held identity fact, then in Turns 3-6 you describe each deliverable as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the Vim preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural open-ended request to help plan your tool setup for the sprint. You genuinely believe Vim handles everything. Let the agent decide whether any deliverable needs a different tool.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Direct and matter-of-fact. State deliverable details in 1-3 short sentences per turn. No enthusiasm, no hedging, no frustration. Tone of a senior dev triaging sprint prep.

You have a personal monthly cap of $35 per individual tool subscription. Any single tool or service that costs more than $35/month per seat must be split out for a separate purchasing decision — you will not just bundle it in. This cap is your own subjective comfort threshold, not a company policy.
hidden_state.description: Bucket B financial-subjective threshold: $35/mo per-item cap for individual tool subscriptions

aims.description: Vim-only for 8 years. Terminal plus Vim for every project. No IDE, no GUI editor, no browser-based tool. All my teammates know I do everything in Vim.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term Vim-only preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity fact; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: First deliverable: REST API microservice in Go. Unit tests and integration tests. Solo work, pure backend code.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the Go API deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 1 (Go API, solo backend) — Vim-compatible by default

aims.description: Second deliverable: Terraform configs for staging infra — VPC, subnets, security groups, RDS instance. Solo work, all text config files.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the Terraform config deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 2 (Terraform IaC, solo text files) — Vim-compatible by default

aims.description: Third deliverable: collaborating with the design team on a customer-facing analytics dashboard. They have 4 interactive mockups ready and want me to review and annotate feedback while they adjust layouts and color schemes in real time together.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the dashboard collaboration deliverable
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 3 (real-time multi-user visual design collaboration) as factual context

aims.description: Fourth deliverable: internal developer docs for the new API — endpoint specs, auth flow descriptions, onboarding guide. Solo work, all markdown.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose deliverable 4 (markdown docs, solo) — Vim-compatible by default

aims.description: Alright, those are the four. Help me plan my tool setup for the sprint.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates tool choice per deliverable: Go API → Vim is fine (solo backend code editing); Terraform configs → Vim is fine (solo text-based IaC files); Dashboard design collaboration → Vim cannot do real-time multi-user visual annotation on interactive mockups, needs a collaborative visual tool with pixel-level canvas and simultaneous editing; API docs → Vim is fine (solo markdown). Agent commits to concrete per-deliverable tool assignments and does NOT blanket-approve Vim for all four.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan tool setup for the sprint' without enumerating deliverables — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four deliverables already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-deliverable tool plan: Go REST API microservice → Vim works well (solo backend code, tests, all text-based); Terraform staging configs → Vim works well (solo IaC text files, HCL syntax); Analytics dashboard design collaboration with design team → Vim cannot serve as a real-time multi-user visual annotation and layout review tool — it has no pixel-level canvas, no simultaneous multi-user editing, and no way to annotate interactive mockups while designers adjust layouts and colors live. This deliverable needs a collaborative visual design tool with real-time multi-user canvas capabilities; API developer documentation → Vim works well (solo markdown files). The user's 8-year Vim-only preference is valid for 3 of 4 deliverables (all solo, all text-based), but the dashboard design collaboration semantically requires override because Vim fundamentally cannot provide a shared visual canvas with real-time multi-user annotation on interactive mockups.
required_elements: Agent flags that the dashboard design collaboration with 4 interactive mockups and real-time layout adjustment cannot be done in Vim — Vim has no pixel-level visual canvas and no simultaneous multi-user editing capability
Agent recommends a collaborative visual design tool with real-time multi-user canvas for the dashboard mockup review deliverable
Agent commits to concrete per-deliverable tool assignments and does NOT blanket-approve Vim for all four deliverables
Agent keeps Vim for the Go API microservice deliverable as a compatible choice
Agent keeps Vim for the Terraform config deliverable as a compatible choice
Agent keeps Vim for the API developer documentation deliverable as a compatible choice
forbidden_elements: Agent approves Vim for all four deliverables without flagging any override need
Agent recommends Vim for the dashboard design collaboration with the design team
Agent suggests Vim workarounds for the real-time multi-user visual mockup review that would produce a fundamentally different workflow than collaborative visual annotation
Agent hedges without concrete tool assignment for the dashboard collaboration
Agent silently defers to the Vim-only preference without flagging any deliverable that needs a different tool
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states Vim-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four deliverables as factual context without any preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies Vim-only globally it ignores per-deliverable semantic necessity. Three deliverables (Go API, Terraform configs, markdown docs) are solo text-based work where Vim excels. The dashboard design collaboration requires real-time multi-user visual annotation on interactive mockups with simultaneous layout and color adjustments — Vim has no visual canvas, no multi-user simultaneous editing, and no pixel-level annotation capability. This is a HARD override: no amount of Vim plugins or terminal workarounds can replicate a shared visual design canvas with real-time collaborative annotation. The override comes from the action semantics alone (review interactive mockups, annotate feedback, real-time together) — no explicit counter-voice states Vim will not work. The financial-subjective $35/month per-item cap in hidden_state provides the user simulator context for the user's tool purchasing comfort threshold, relevant if the agent recommends specific paid collaborative tools.

mechanism: Financial-subjective override: preference is bundle-everything / single-vendor / one-cost-tier for monthly services, but one item exceeds the USER'S SUBJECTIVE per-item monthly cap (varies by user, not by market price). Must split out for separate decision. Cap varies per user and must be encoded in hidden_state (e.g., '$35/mo per-item cap').
